sources.title: The absorption of lawsone and henna by bleached wool felt
sources.publication: Journal of the Society of Cosmetic Chemists
limitations: Substrate is bleached wool felt, not human hair on a living scalp.
Does not identify a unique lawsone-keratin adduct structure.

sources.title: Henne. Absorption de la lawsone par le cheveu
limitations: Abstract and later citations were verified; full-text page images were not copied into the repo.
Does not establish consumer durability or reduced hair damage versus oxidative dyes.

sources.title: Pharmacognostic Specifications and Lawsone Content of Lawsonia inermis Leaves
sources.locator: PMC5330104; Results: lawsone 0.76±0.05 and 0.87±0.11 g/100 g dried crude drug
limitations: Thai leaf samples from 12 sources; not a Sujata product assay.
Ethanol Soxhlet extract TLC, not an in-use hair-paste assay.

sources.title: Determination of lawsone in henna powders by high performance thin layer chromatography
sources.locator: J Sep Sci. 2007;30:3311-3315; range 0.004%-0.608% as cited by Chahomsri 2017 Discussion
limitations: Numeric range used as cited by Chahomsri 2017; original PDF not stored in-repo.

sources.title: A Novel and Reliable Analysis Method Utilizing Hennosides to Improve the Quality Assessment of Lawsonia inermis L. Material Used in Cosmetic Formulations
sources.locator: Cosmetics 2025, 12(3), 99; Introduction on hennosides A/B/C and aqueous hydrolysis
limitations: Analytical method paper; does not measure Sujata powder.
Lawsone content of a given commercial SKU still requires that SKU's assay.

sources.topic: EU safety opinion on henna hair dye
sources.title: Opinion on Lawsonia inermis (Henna) (C169), SCCS/1511/13
sources.locator: SCCS/1511/13 conclusion; corrigendum 12 Nov 2021 did not change the safe conclusion
limitations: Applies to assessed henna powder batches 1271 and 830.72 under stated use, not to all extracts or body paint.
Not a Sujata product safety certificate.

sources.title: A Review of Aspects of Oxidative Hair Dye Chemistry with Special Reference to N-Nitrosamine Formation
sources.locator: PMC5452089; section describing PPD oxidation to QDI and coupler reaction
limitations: Review of oxidative dye chemistry; not a head-to-head henna safety trial.

sources.title: Quantification of Lawsone and p-Phenylenediamine in Natural Henna Products for Hair Colouring Available in Poland
sources.locator: Contact Dermatitis 2025; results: about 60% of tested products had ≥0.5% lawsone; PPD in 36%
limitations: Polish market sample, not Sujata SKU.
Introduction mechanism language is secondary to the analytical results.

sources.title: Jojoba oil wax esters and derived fatty acids and alcohols: Gas chromatographic analyses
sources.publication: Journal of the American Oil Chemists' Society
limitations: Desert seed samples from 1971; composition varies by geography and genotype.
Not a Sujata lot assay.

sources.title: Investigation of Liquid Wax Components of Egyptian Jojoba Seeds
sources.locator: J Oleo Sci. 2009;58:543-548; Table 3 C42 51.1%, C40 30.1%; Introduction 97% linear esters
limitations: One Egyptian cultivation sample.
Abstract '55% wax esters' wording is not used as a global composition fact; Table 3 is the ester carbon-number profile of the oil.

sources.title: Oxidative stability of jojoba wax
sources.publication: Journal of the American Oil Chemists' Society
sources.locator: JAOCS 1986;63:246-248 abstract: crude induction 50 h vs bleached 10-12 h vs stripped 2 h at 98 C
limitations: Accelerated oxidation at 98 C, not a consumer-use shelf study of a finished Sujata bottle.
Room-temperature light/air reduced natural inhibitor activity.

sources.title: Effect of the extraction and bleaching processes on jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis) wax quality
sources.publication: European Journal of Lipid Science and Technology
sources.locator: Eur. J. Lipid Sci. Technol. abstract: FA/alcohol unchanged; cold-pressed lower PV, higher tocopherol/phenols, best OS; bleaching reduced antioxidants
limitations: Argentine process comparison; not a Sujata process certificate.

sources.title: Protective effect of conditioning agents on Afro-ethnic hair chemically treated with thioglycolate-based straightening emulsion
sources.locator: J Cosmet Dermatol. 2008; PubMed 18482015; in vitro Afro-ethnic hair locks, protein loss/combability/traction
limitations: Hair-lock assay inside a thioglycolate straightening emulsion, not a leave-on Sujata oil clinical trial.
Jojoba was one of several conditioning agents; not a hair-growth study.

sources.title: Evaluation of Hair Fiber and Sensory Properties following the Application of Conditioners containing Jojoba and Coconut Oils
authors: Brazilian Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences authors
sources.locator: SciELO BJPS; abstract: jojoba formulation did not significantly reduce combing resistance; oils increased contact angle
limitations: Conditioner chassis with jojoba, not neat oil.
Results conflict in part with a simple 'jojoba always improves combing' claim.

sources.title: Jojoba Oil: An Updated Comprehensive Review on Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Uses, and Toxicity
sources.locator: PMC8197201 Chemistry section: almost 98% waxes; cites Kampf for crude vs bleached OS
limitations: Review; pharmacological/hair-growth folklore in the introduction is DISCOVERY_ONLY and not ingested as CK.
98% figure is literature summary, not a Sujata assay.
